transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I barely sleep right anymore. I'll just lie there at night... hearing the rain or thinking about the bluff giving way. And then when I finally do pass out, I wake up all sweaty from these dreams. By the time I show up to my shift at the call center, I feel like I never even slept.
Do you feel anxious or on edge during the day, outside of when you're trying to sleep?

I don't really know if I'd call it anxious, exactly. I just feel... tired, mostly. I mean, my job is just answering phones all day, so I'm sitting there trying to focus on what the customer is saying, but my brain is just foggy. I don't really feel on edge, just worn out from not sleeping.
You mentioned having dreams that make you wake up sweaty, are these dreams scary or disturbing?

Yeah, they are. They're usually about the landslide. But it's not just the dreams, honestly. Even when I'm awake, stuff pops in my head out of nowhere. Like... I'll just be sitting at my desk with my headset on, and suddenly I hear the sound of the rocks sliding, or I feel like my leg is stuck under me again. Just for a minute, it feels like I'm right back on that trail instead of at work.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations because they remind you of the landslide?

Yeah, definitely. I won't go anywhere near the coast trails now. I just can't do it. And... I've actually been dodging texts from my old hiking buddies, too. Even just the thought of talking about going out there, or talking to them about it, it just makes my chest tighten up. So I just avoid it altogether.
Are there any specific things, like TV shows or news articles, that you also try to avoid because they remind you of the landslide?

No, not really. I mean, I don't go out of my way to avoid TV shows or the news or anything like that. If something comes on, I just watch it or change the channel like normal. It's really just the actual trails and talking to those friends that I stay away from.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the landslide happened?
This has been going on for about four months now. It started right after I got trapped when that bluff trail collapsed.
Do you try to push away or avoid thinking about the landslide when memories of it come to mind?
No, not really. I mean, if a memory pops up, I just kind of let it happen. I don't really try to block it out or push it away. It's just... there.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy before the landslide happened?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still like doing the stuff I usually do, like playing video games and hanging out with my other friends. I just don't want to go hiking anymore, but everything else is pretty much the same.
Do you find yourself being easily startled by small noises or movements?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, if someone drops something really loud, I might jump a little, just like anyone else would. But small noises or movements... nah, they don't really bother me.
Do you often find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats in your daily life?

No, I don't think so. I just kind of go about my normal day. I'm not, like, looking over my shoulder all the time or expecting something bad to happen when I'm just walking down the street or at work. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm on the lookout like that.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened during the landslide when those memories come to your mind?

No, not really. I mean, if a memory of the landslide pops up, I just... I don't try to push it away or anything. It happened, you know? So if I think about it, I just think about it for a minute and then move on with my day. I don't actively try to block it out of my head.
Have you been feeling sad, hopeless, or depressed since the landslide happened?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, obviously it wasn't a great thing to go through, but... I don't feel depressed or hopeless about it. I'm just waking up and going to work and doing my thing like normal, really. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm feeling sad.
How many hours of sleep do you typically get each night?

I don't really get a lot of sleep anymore. That's actually why I came in. I'll just lie there at night, and if I hear rain, or... I just start thinking about the bluff giving way. And then when I finally do pass out, I end up waking up all sweaty from these dreams. By the time I have to show up at the call center, I feel like I never even slept at all. So, honestly, not many hours.
How many nights a week do you have trouble sleeping due to thoughts or memories of the landslide?

Like I was just saying, it's pretty much most nights. I'd say... probably five or six nights a week. I barely get any normal sleep anymore because I'm just lying there thinking about the bluff or waking up from those dreams. So yeah, almost every single night.
Have you avoided other activities besides hiking since the landslide happened?

Yeah, I mean... I definitely won't go anywhere near the coast trails now. And I actually dodge texts from my hiking buddies, too. Just... even talking about going out there with them makes my chest tighten up. So I just avoid them altogether.
Have you avoided any social activities or gatherings because they remind you of the landslide or the friends you used to hike with?

Yeah, like I was just saying, I pretty much avoid any get-togethers with that group. I dodge all their texts, so I definitely don't go to any gatherings with them. Just thinking about seeing them or going anywhere near those coast trails makes my chest tighten right up. So, yeah, I just stay away from all of it.
Have you avoided other places or situations besides the coast trails and talking to your hiking buddies because they remind you of the landslide?

Um, no, not really. It's mostly just... just the trails and those friends, like I said. I still go to work and do my regular stuff around town, so I can't really think of anything else I've been staying away from.
Would you say that avoiding the coast trails and your hiking buddies is causing significant problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah, it actually is. Um, at work... my performance has slipped enough recently that I missed some important CRM notes on an account. I ended up getting written up after a call escalated, which really sucks because I'm worried I just blew my chance at moving up toward team lead. And then... I don't know, I'm just so exhausted all the time that I've fallen way behind on studying for my GED. So between that and just completely avoiding the guys I used to hike with, it's definitely messing with my daily life right now.
